claims.statement: If one grounded physical relation occurrence and all constitutive signature facts are faithfully included in several independently actual token organizations, the one occurrence is a member of every such token; membership multiplicity does not multiply occurrence count.
claims.domain: one actual episode, finitely many declared actual process tokens and faithful token-relative organizations
premises: actual token status for every selected token
claims.proof_or_source: definition expansion; UCT I v1.2 §§2.1-2.5 and TA25 D1
counterexamples_or_limits: a view is not automatically an actual token
omitted endpoints or boundary mechanisms defeat membership
claims.thought_experiment_role: TE1 and TE5 show multiple membership without duplication or local erasure

claims.statement: Equal relation type, carried value, local views, whole output and report do not identify same-occurrence equivalence or the cross-scale incidence profile.
claims.domain: shared one-occurrence and copied two-occurrence finite architectures
premises: declared occurrence identifiers and membership matrices
claims.proof_or_source: explicit countermodel; 16 crossed configurations and exact assertions
counterexamples_or_limits: additional occurrence-sensitive evidence can distinguish the models
not a claim of complete organizational equality
claims.thought_experiment_role: TE2 blocks value-based and report-based occurrence identity

claims.statement: A synchronizer can propagate a perturbation between distinct copies, but the synchronizer is an additional whole-organization relation and does not make the copies numerically one occurrence.
claims.domain: directed two-copy finite architecture with declared synchronizer and clamp
premises: synchronizer represented in the whole signature
claims.proof_or_source: direct substitution with synchronizer active versus clamped
counterexamples_or_limits: if the synchronizer cannot be isolated, shared versus copied remains underidentified
intervention fidelity remains an actual-application obligation
claims.thought_experiment_role: TE2 and TE3 distinguish copied equality from shared occurrence membership

claims.statement: For every selected independently actual token, C1 transports each admitted member occurrence to a token-relative experiential structural counterpart; a grounded coherent overlap diagram relates the images without thereby proving a numerically single phenomenal event or exclusive subject.
claims.domain: same episode, actual token family, complete compatible token-relative signatures and grounded overlap maps
claims.proof_or_source: tokenwise isomorphism transport plus inherited coherent overlap construction
counterexamples_or_limits: no cross-token numerical identity from tokenwise C1 alone
claims.thought_experiment_role: TE1-TE5 preserve token relativity, copying and nonexclusive overlap

claims.statement: The sum of token memberships of an occurrence is not the number of physical occurrences and cannot be used as a consciousness amount, subject count or richness score.
claims.domain: cross-scale incidence matrices with grounded occurrence equivalence classes
premises: occurrence classes are fixed by physical identity
counterexamples_or_limits: membership count can still be a useful organizational descriptor
claims.thought_experiment_role: TE4 exposes value copies across a human-realized agent
